Liraglutide was recently approved for the treatment of obesity in adolescents >12 years. Liraglutide is a glucagon-like receptor 1
agonist, which reduces food intake. In adults, treatment is associated with 6% of weight loss, 13% reduction in major adverse
cardiovascular events and a 15% reduction in all-cause mortality (González-Muniesa et al., 2017).
Other medications that have been used off-label for the treatment of obesity in children include topiramate.
More trials are needed to better understand the efﬁcacy and safety of these medications for the treatment of pediatric obesity.
Surgical treatment
There are few available data regarding bariatric surgery in children and adolescents and they are limited to the publication of case
studies and expert consensus statements, with no controlled studies or data regarding the long-term results. The retrospective series
analyzed by the Collaborative Group for the Study of Pediatric Bariatric Surgery is based on gastric bypass surgery, the most used
technique in the United States, whereas in Europe and Australia adjustable gastric banding has been more widely used. Thus,
speciﬁc recommendations regarding its use in children and adolescents cannot be made, and it should be limited to extreme cases
and performed only in highly specialized centers (Kumar and Kelly, 2017; Styne et al., 2017).
